meta.title: New Intake Platform: Go-live Readiness Review
meta.subtitle: Five of Six Criteria Met, One Fix Before Nov 17
meta.decision: Approve go-live on Nov 17 once interface testing passes
meta.big_idea: The platform is ready except interface testing, which finishes Nov 10, so we can go live on Nov 17.
meta.notes: Synthetic example data for the skill self-test. Not real results.

slides.title: Once Interface Testing Passes, We Are Ready to Go Live on Nov 17
points: Five of six go-live criteria are met
Pilot clinics book first visits three days sooner
slides.notes: Lead with the answer: one open criterion, with a date, then the ask.

slides.title: Five of Six Go-live Criteria Are Met
slides.notes: Interface testing slipped one week because a vendor test window moved; the new date still leaves a week of buffer.

slides.title: Pilot Clinics Already Beat the Launch Targets
slides.notes: These are the launch targets the committee set in August. Pilot results clear every one, so the remaining risk sits in the interface, not the workflow.

slides.title: The Platform Runs on Four Layers, and One Is Still in Test

nodes.label: Referral Sources
nodes.detail: Physician offices, hospitals and the patient portal send referrals

nodes.label: Routing Rules
nodes.detail: Send each referral to the right team

nodes.label: Scheduling Interface
nodes.detail: Books the visit and stays in testing until Nov 10

slides.alt: Four stacked layers from referral sources to the scheduling interface, with the interface layer highlighted.
slides.notes: Only the bottom layer, the interface to the clinic scheduling system, is still in test.

slides.title: Patients Start Treatment Sooner
slides.label: Faster to First Visit
slides.text: Pilot clinics, compared with the six months before the pilot.
slides.notes: Breather: this is why the date matters to patients.

slides.title: Defects Fell From Twelve to Two in Three Test Cycles
slides.takeaway: The two open defects are cosmetic; neither blocks scheduling.
slides.notes: Both open defects are label wording issues, fixed in the Nov 7 build.

slides.title: Schedulers Book From One Screen
points: Referral, insurance and routing in one view
Booking writes straight to the clinic system

visual.alt: Scheduler screen with referral details, insurance status and a book button.

slides.notes: This is the screen schedulers trained on; the interface work makes the book button write to the clinic system.

slides.title: Go-live Takes Four Steps, Starting With Interface Testing

steps.label: Pass Interface Testing
steps.detail: Integration team finishes testing by Nov 10

steps.label: Switch On by Region
steps.detail: West and Central switch on first, on Nov 17

slides.notes: Step one is the only open dependency; the other three steps are scheduled and staffed.

slides.title: Most Remaining Test Cases Cover the Interface
slides.takeaway: Finishing the interface cases closes almost three quarters of the remaining test work.
slides.alt: Bar chart of open test cases by area; interface has the most at 18.
slides.notes: Routing, form and report cases are low risk and scheduled this week.

slides.title: Three Questions the Committee Will Likely Ask

pairs.q: What if interface testing slips again?
pairs.a: We keep the old booking path live and move go-live one week; no clinic is affected.

pairs.q: Who supports clinics on day one?
pairs.a: The service desk plus two analysts on site in each first-wave region.

pairs.q: How will we know it is working?
pairs.a: Daily dashboard of bookings, errors and time to first visit for two weeks.

slides.notes: Anticipate these so the decision is not delayed by follow-up questions.

slides.title: Decision Needed: Approve Go-live for Nov 17

asks.action: Approve go-live, conditional on Nov 10 testing

slides.notes: Ask for a conditional approval so the Nov 10 result triggers go-live without another meeting.
